key_insight: In Ba3HoRu2O9, low-energy spin waves and higher-energy features arise from overlapping magnetic, crystal-field, and phonon excitations, with the ~39 meV band reflecting mixed contributions rather than a single origin.
engineering_relevance: Disentangling these coupled excitations gives a microscopic basis for tuning spin-dipole coupling and functional responses in correlated 4d-4f multiferroics.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering mapped excitation energies and dispersion.
Linear spin-wave and crystal-field (Stevens) analysis assigned magnetic and Ho3+ transitions.
Raman spectroscopy and machine-learned force-field phonon calculations identified overlapping optical phonons.
evidence_signal: The dispersive mode below 6.2 meV matches spin-wave theory, while broad INS features near 20, 39, 70, and 90 meV persist above the magnetic ordering temperature and align with calculated crystal-field and phonon energies.
watch_item: The high-energy INS bands are overlapping and broad, so assigning a single microscopic origin to the ~39 meV feature remains inherently ambiguous.
paper_title: Interplay of Spin Waves, Crystal-Field Excitations, and Phonons in Multiferroic Ba3HoRu2O9 revealed by Inelastic Neutron Scattering, Crystal-Field Analysis, and Machine-Learned Phonon Calculations
